breakdown.description: 300 nm light has photon energy of about 4.13 eV, below a work function of 4.8 eV, so photoemission cannot occur.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification correctly uses 240 nm light (matching the ground truth) instead of the incorrect 300 nm. It computes the photon energy as ~5.17 eV, which exceeds the work function of 4.8 eV, correctly concluding that photoemission does occur. This directly fixes the inconsistency where 300 nm light (4.13 eV) would have been below the work function and no emission would occur.
